- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days.
- Sentiment history with alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67) triggers model overfitting; smooth forecast by averaging last 3 values before adjustment.
